criteria.evidence: Purdue ArcGIS BuildingShapesZip4 FID 773 identifies Zeta Tau Alpha at 118 Waldron St (SOZTA). I independently inverse-projected the raw EPSG:3857 ring and transformed it with the repository local approximation, then rebuilt the saved shell base ring from the fresh Blender extraction. Shape IoU=0.999999969, area 744.706199 vs 744.706208 m², centroid error 0.00000003 m. This verifies transfer of the public GIS ring, not a surveyed structural wall line.

The model keeps campus-coordinate geometry and records origin XY [-320.5144435379624, -187.07450048567304] m, within 0.000000 m of the transformed GIS centroid. The outline supports the plan dimensions; facade direction is plausible from the chapter-house photo and saved reference, but the standalone candidate has not yet been checked as an installed instance in the current master. The local geographic conversion is approximate.

Fresh asset bounds give a maximum Z of 11.91 m; the R2 report now correctly describes this as the model's estimated peak, removing the former 12.5 m discrepancy. ArcGIS Extrution=12 is undocumented, while NUM_LEVELS and CountOfFLO are 1, so actual stories/height remain unverified. The 2022 official photo supports a pitched dark roof and portico silhouette; the multiple dormers/roof layout are modeled interpretation.

The R2 front render now shows the ZTA mark on the outward-facing pediment plane, resolving the R1 occlusion. Red brick, pale trim, a white columned portico, cross-muntin windows, and dark pitched roof broadly match the official 2022 chapter-house photo. The model is stylized, has fewer/simpler facade details than the photo, and its windows are layered over a continuous shell rather than cut-through openings.

criteria.criterion: Technical integrity, materials, interior, and evidence
criteria.evidence: Fresh Blender 5.2.3 LTS process reopened the exact SHA 1e9b54a032ac508e3e473e1757b6edce6ee8724b581c884d54e984572ed8a7af. The stable scene/collection has 563 objects (562 meshes plus the ZTA lettering), 13 named materials, no materialless meshes, and 4 image dependencies, all packed. The interior collection has 112 schematic objects including three floor plates, a corridor, dining furniture, bedrooms/stair furniture; no measured plan or bathrooms/partition layout is verified.
